name: How do contractors match older or discontinued trim profiles?

mainEntity.name: How do contractors match older or discontinued trim profiles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Matching existing trim requires identifying the wood species, dimensions, and profile contours before purchasing stock. In older homes across Denver, Centennial, and Parker, original baseboards and casings often feature custom millwork profiles not sold in modern big-box stores. When repairing a segment, a finish carpenter measures the depth, height, and edge curves, then checks regional lumber suppliers for matches. If a profile is discontinued, an experienced carpenter can combine multiple stock moldings—such as a flat baseboard with a base cap molding—to replicate the historic design closely.
acceptedAnswer.description: Contractors measure the exact profile curves and dimensions, source architectural lumber suppliers, or build up multiple stock pieces to accurately mirror discontinued designs.
